content.body:
I lost 24 lbs on my weight loss jab, and completely wrecked my digestion doing it.

At first I didn't care.

I'd fought my weight for years, and suddenly the thing I'd wanted for so long was actually happening.

The scales were going down, my jeans were looser, people were asking if I'd lost weight.

And for the first time in years I actually wanted to be in the photo.

Then my stomach started fighting back.

It started small.

Feeling stuffed after half a meal. "That's just how the jab works," I told myself.

Then came the constipation.

The bloating.

The gas.

And that horrible heavy brick feeling, where I'd eat lunch at 1pm and still feel it sitting there at 7 that night.

And the more weight I lost, the worse it got.

I'd wake up and see the progress, waist smaller, clothes looser.

Then I'd eat one tiny meal and by dinner my stomach was sticking out so far I looked six months pregnant.

I stood in the bathroom one night, pulling my shirt tight against my belly, thinking:

"I've lost 24 pounds, so why do I still look bigger?"

That was when the excitement wore off.

I was getting thinner and feeling awful.

Barely eating, constantly full, days without properly going to the toilet.

And every time I thought about stopping the jab, I'd look at the scales, see another pound gone, and tell myself…

"just deal with it, this is the price of finally being thin."

So I kept injecting, and I kept feeling worse.

I started planning my whole life around my stomach.

Barely eating all day before dinner out, terrified one normal meal would destroy me.

I stopped wearing anything fitted, because even though I'd lost weight, the bloating could make my stomach look bigger than before I started.

That was the part I wasn’t prepared for… The scales going down while my stomach looked bigger.

So I tried every hack and piece of advice I could find online.

Water, fibre, probiotics, magnesium, prunes, walking after meals.

The fibre was the worst of the lot.

Everyone said "constipated? eat more fibre."

So I forced it in, and every night I felt like I was going to explode.

Sitting on the sofa with my trousers undone, rubbing my belly, wondering how I could eat so little and still feel this full.

Then came the night that broke me.

I was out at dinner with my husband.

Before the jab I'd have finished the whole meal, tonight I was lucky if I managed to eat a third of it.

And by the time we got home I was in agony.

I ran upstairs, threw off my clothes and curled up in a ball on my bed.

My stomach was huge, you could see it through my dress, and the pain was unbearable.

I looked more pregnant than thin.

My husband looked at me and said, "Is all this really worth it if you're this miserable?"

And I thought: he's right…

What is the f*cking point of losing all this weight if I have to hide my stomach every single night?

That was the first time I seriously thought about quitting the injections.

Not because they weren't working, but because I didn't know how much longer I could live like this.

That night, lying in bed, I started doom-scrolling GLP-1 threads on Reddit.

And I wasn't alone… Woman after woman saying the exact same thing.

“Lost the weight, wrecked their stomach”

“Scared to eat before leaving the house.”

“Days without going to the toilet.”

“Loving the weight results but not knowing how much longer they could keep living in misery.”

Then I found a post from a pharmacist, and the first line stopped me dead:

"Most women on GLP 1 jabs are trying to fix this from the wrong end."

She explained most women think the problem is simple: I'm constipated, I need to get it all out.

So they reach for laxatives, fibre, magnesium, anything to make themselves go.

That was exactly what I'd been doing.

But she said the constipation is the LAST part of the problem, the real problem starts hours earlier, much higher up.

The jab doesn't just kill your appetite, it slows your whole gut down.

So food that used to move straight through now sits there for hours in the wrong part of the gut called the small intestine.

And when it sits that high up, for too long, where it was never meant to stay, gut bacteria get the time to ferment it.

That fermentation process is supposed to happen much lower down in your gut where there the correct gut bacteria lived and where there is space for this to happen.

But when this process happens in the small intestine where there is no room for the gas build up and bloating, it becomes painfully unbearable.

That fermentation is the gas, the pressure, the sulphur burps, and that brick-under-the-ribs feeling like the meal you ate six hours ago is still there.

The gut gets inflamed and jammed, and everything backs up behind it.

I stared at my phone thinking, That's exactly it.

For months I thought my problem was "I can't go to the toilet."

But that was just the bit I could see at the end.

And suddenly I understood why everything I'd tried made me worse.

The laxatives only reach the lower gut, so they completely miss the food stuck fermenting higher up.

The fibre just piled more into an already-jammed system, more fuel for the fire.

The probiotics dumped even more bacteria high up where they didn't belong, making the fermentation worse.

And it was all happening in the wrong part of my gut which is why the pain was unbearable.

So I replied under her post: "Okay, so how do I stop all this without coming off the GLP 1 jab?"

Because that was the one thing I would not do.

I'd lost 24 lbs, my appetite was finally under control and I wasn't willing to give that back without a fight.

Her reply was simple.

She said forget everything you've been doing, there are only three things that actually matter, and they all work together.

First, you have to get the food moving again, that's the whole root of the problem.

The food sitting there for hours is what starts the entire mess.

Ginger's one of the only things clinically shown to actually do that.

It gets your stomach pushing food through again instead of letting it stall and ferment.

But moving it isn't enough on its own, because if it's not being broken down properly it'll still sit heavy and rot where it sits.

That's why you need a high quality digestive enzymes to do this.

Bromelain which comes from pineapples is the best for this.

it breaks a meal down so it clears instead of festering.

And then there's the part I cared about most…The gas.

That trapped, clenched, bulging pressure that had me undoing my trousers on the sofa every night.

She said you need Peppermint and fennel to relax the gut muscle and let all of that finally release, instead of it building until I felt like I'd explode.

Three things, working together, fixing the actual chain reaction from the slowed gut

The only problem is that I now needed four different ingredients at the right doses

And my bathroom cabinet already looked like a chemist's shelf.

I was done playing scientist.

So I asked if I could pay her to help me put it all together in the correct doses.

She replied: "You don't need to pay me. Take a look at this."

Underneath was a link to a product called BloatBurn by Neuaura.

I opened it and went through the ingredients and it had everything she had mentioned in her reply.

It was built for exactly what was happening to my digestion while the jab did its job.

So I ordered it that night.

The first changes were small.

A few days in, I ate dinner and realised an hour later I wasn't sitting there rubbing my stomach wondering how long it would sit there.

The meal just felt easier.

By the end of week one, the brick feeling wasn't taking over my whole evening, and going to the toilet started feeling normal again.

By week two, my stomach wasn't blowing up every afternoon.

My waistband wasn't murdering me by dinner.

And I'd stopped being scared of food.

Then one night my husband asked if I wanted to go out for dinner again.

The last time flashed straight into my head.

Me curled on the bed, my dress stretched over my stomach, him asking if it was worth it.

Normally I'd start planning.

Skip lunch?

What's safe to eat?

Wear something loose?

But this time I just went.

I ate, we talked, we laughed, we came home and had a fumble around in the bedroom.

And while I was getting ready for bed I realised I hadn't thought about my stomach once all night.

Because that was all I'd ever wanted.

I didn't want to quit the jab.

I didn't want my appetite back.

I didn't want the 24 lbs back.

I just wanted to enjoy the weight loss results without feeling like I'd destroyed my gut to get them.

So if you're on GLP 1 jabs and the weight is finally coming off.

But food sits inside you for hours, you're backed up for days, your stomach blows up every afternoon.

and you're throwing fibre, probiotics and laxatives at it without ever feeling normal.

Stop. Because you've been fighting the wrong end of this the entire time.

It was never about forcing yourself to go to the toilet.

It was food sitting too long, fermenting too high up, and everything backing up behind it.

Clear that, and the rest sorts itself out.

You don’t have to spend every evening curled up, undoing your jeans, wondering if you've wrecked your gut for good.

You can keep the weight loss… You just don't have to keep the misery.

Bloatburn even comes with a 90-day money back guarantee, so you can try it and see for yourself.

That's why BloatBurn made sense to me and I hope it helps you too.
